hint_ladder.title: Ano ba ang 'mitigate'?
hint_ladder.text: Sa balita, 'mitigating measures' laban sa bagyo—ibig sabihin, pampabawas ng pinsala. Ang ibig sabihin: to lessen or lighten.

hint_ladder.title: Synonym = kapareho ng ibig sabihin
hint_ladder.text: Ang hinahanap ay salitang pare-pareho ang kahulugan: 'bawasan ang bigat o hirap.' 'Yan ang itutok mo.

hint_ladder.title: Tanggalin ang mali
hint_ladder.text: Intensify at Aggravate parehong 'palalain.' Complicate ibig sabihin 'guluhin.' I-cross out na agad—sila'y kabaligtaran.

hint_ladder.title: Isipin ang doktor
hint_ladder.text: Kapag may sakit, ang gamot ay para i-alleviate ang pain—pinagaan. Same ng mitigate. Kaya C ang sagot.

A.text: You might have chosen A because 'intensify' sounds like strong action, but it means to make stronger—the opposite of mitigate.

B.text: You might have chosen B because 'aggravate' is often paired with 'mitigate' in legal terms, but aggravate means to worsen, not lessen.

C.text: Correct. Alleviate and mitigate both mean to make something less severe, sharing the idea of easing a burden.

D.text: You might have chosen D because mitigating might involve steps, but 'complicate' means to make tangled, not to reduce severity.

next_time_rule: When looking for a synonym of 'mitigate,' remember 'ibsan'—to lessen. If a choice means to worsen, cross it out. Focus on lightening the load.
deconstruct_text:
Imagine you're in a barangay after a typhoon. The LGU distributes relief goods to mitigate the hunger of affected families. 'Mitigate' means to lessen the suffering—parang pagbawas ng bigat ng problema. In tagalog, 'ibsan' o 'pawiin.'

Now, options: Intensify and Aggravate mean to make stronger or worse—parang dinadagdagan ang hirap. Complicate means to make gulo. Only Alleviate does the same: pinagagaan ang pasanin. Kaya ang sagot ay C.
